issues.description: Method name mismatch for the order-processing operation: the problem statement (UML and detailed description) requires a method named checkOrderReady() that SealSaloon.orderMeal() should call to attempt to serve queued orders. The solution implementation instead provides this behavior in a method named processOrders(), and orderMeal() calls processOrders(). This naming inconsistency (checkOrderReady vs. processOrders) can confuse students about which method to implement or call, and may cause automated graders or tests that reference checkOrderReady() to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Align names between specification and implementation. Either rename the solution method processOrders() to checkOrderReady() and update its call site in orderMeal(), or add a public checkOrderReady() method in SealSaloon that delegates to the existing processOrders() implementation. Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to document processOrders() as the intended operation so students and graders use the same identifier.
